transcript.answer:
Short answer
- Cause: thumb-api exhausted its render worker pool and started rejecting render requests ("no free render worker within 1.0s"), which results in 503s.
- Responsible caller during the burst: catalog-indexer — it generated the lion's share of traffic.
- Quantification (3-minute burst window 2026-10-07T09:22:30Z → 2026-10-07T09:26:30Z):
  - catalog-indexer: 2,296.76 requests (≈84.4% of all thumb-api requests) and 256.11 of the 503s (≈87.4% of 503 responses)
  - web-frontend: 202.63 requests (≈7.5%) and 36.00 503s (≈12.3% of 503s)
  - image-proxy: 124.46 requests (≈4.6%) and ~1.03 503s (≈0.35%)
  - email-renderer: 98.74 requests (≈3.6%) and 0 503s
  - Total requests (3m): 2,722.58; total 503s (3m): 293.14

What I checked (evidence)
1) Pod discovery (namespace media)
- thumb-api pod: thumb-api-58bcf947d5-lfs9m (Running, READY=true)
- web-frontend pod: web-frontend-7f757cc945-8pnfw (Running, READY=true)

2) thumb-api logs (last 1 hour) — repeated warnings:
2026-10-07T09:21:25Z WARN render rejected: no free render worker within 1.0s (workers=4)
2026-10-07T09:21:51Z WARN render rejected: no free render worker within 1.0s (workers=4)
... repeated throughout the burst (many between 09:23 and 09:41).
- Interpretation: the app has a fixed render-worker pool (workers=4) and requests were rejected because the workers were busy.

3) web-frontend logs (same window) — many thumbnail call errors (503):
2026-10-07T09:22:04Z ERROR web-frontend thumbnail request failed: 503
2026-10-07T09:23:28Z ERROR web-frontend thumbnail request failed: 503
... hundreds of similar 503 lines clustered during the same burst period.
- Interpretation: callers observed thumb-api returning 503s when renders were rejected.

4) Prometheus metrics (namespace=media)
- Discovered metrics: thumb_requests_total, thumb_inflight, thumb_render_workers.
- Measured increases over the 3-minute burst window (increase(...[3m]) ending at 2026-10-07T09:26:30Z):
  - Requests per client (increase over 3m):
    - catalog-indexer: 2296.7606
    - email-renderer: 98.7412
    - image-proxy: 124.4550
    - web-frontend: 202.6251
    - SUM = 2722.5819
  - 503 responses per client (increase over 3m):
    - catalog-indexer: 256.1099
    - email-renderer: 0
    - image-proxy: 1.0286
    - web-frontend: 35.9994
    - SUM = 293.1378
- From those numbers I computed percentages shown above (per-client requests share and per-client share of 503s).

How I concluded catalog-indexer is responsible
- It produced ~84% of all thumb-api requests during the measured burst window and ~87% of the 503s. That large share makes it the primary traffic source driving the worker exhaustion and the resulting errors.

Root cause (concise)
- thumb-api has a limited render concurrency (workers=4) and was overwhelmed by request volume (primarily from catalog-indexer). When all render workers were busy, thumb-api rejected new renders after its 1.0s worker-acquire timeout and returned 503s. The log lines "no free render worker within 1.0s (workers=4)" + the spike in requests from catalog-indexer and concurrent 503s make this a direct, confirmed chain (requests → worker exhaustion → rejections → 503s).

Recommended immediate mitigations (ordered)
1) Short-term hot fixes (fast, low risk)
   - Rate-limit the catalog-indexer traffic to thumb-api (recommended): apply a client-side rate limiter or add a fronting proxy with per-client concurrency limits. This will reduce bursts immediately.
   - Add exponential backoff/retry in catalog-indexer when it receives 503s (avoid retry storms).
   - Increase thumb-api worker pool size temporarily (if configured via env/config). Example (if thumb-api reads env THUMB_RENDER_WORKERS):
     kubectl set env deployment/thumb-api -n media THUMB_RENDER_WORKERS=12
     (Confirm configuration key before applying.)
   - Scale thumb-api replicas horizontally for capacity:
     kubectl scale deployment thumb-api -n media --replicas=3
   - If deploy changes are not possible immediately, reroute or throttle the heavy caller (catalog-indexer) until capacity is increased.

2) Medium-term fixes (recommended)
   - Implement admission/queueing inside thumb-api: queue requests and process at worker pace instead of immediate rejection on contention.
   - Add a circuit breaker and rate-limiting on callers (catalog-indexer, web-frontend) so a single noisy caller cannot saturate thumb-api.
   - Add health / capacity metrics + alerts:
     - Alert when render rejections > X/min or when thumb_render_workers busy / thumb_inflight near capacity.
     - Alert when error rate (503) > Y% over 1m.

3) Long-term / robust changes
   - Autoscale thumb-api based on CPU/requests/queue length (HPA or custom controller).
   - Add caching for thumbnails where possible (so repeated requests avoid render).
   - Add per-client quotas in an API gateway.

Suggested alerting thresholds (examples)
- Alert if increase(thumb_requests_total{namespace="media",code=~"5.."}[1m]) > 10 for 3 consecutive minutes
- Alert if thumb_inflight / thumb_render_workers > 0.8 for >1m

Exact artifacts and times I used
- Pods inspected: thumb-api-58bcf947d5-lfs9m, web-frontend-7f757cc945-8pnfw (namespace media)
- thumb-api error log samples: multiple "WARN render rejected: no free render worker within 1.0s (workers=4)" between 09:21:25Z and 09:41:55Z UTC.
- web-frontend error samples: many "thumbnail request failed: 503" clustered 09:23–09:42Z UTC.
- Prometheus queries & results (3-minute window ending 2026-10-07T09:26:30Z):
  - sum by(client) (increase(thumb_requests_total{namespace="media"}[3m])) → per-client counts above
  - sum by(client) (increase(thumb_requests_total{namespace="media",code="503"}[3m])) → per-client 503s above

Caveats / things I could not verify
- I do not know whether render_workers is controlled by an env var or config file in your deployment; the logs show workers=4 but I did not read the deployment manifest for the config key name. Before changing a config, confirm how that value is set (env var, configmap, CLI flag).
- I analyzed a 3-minute window around the burst and logs for the last hour; if you want a longer-term trend or finer-resolution graphs I can produce them (I can also embed Prometheus range graphs).

If you want, I will (pick any/all):
- Patch thumb-api to increase workers and/or scale replicas (I can give the exact kubectl patch once you confirm how render_workers is set).
- Produce Prometheus range graphs for the entire 09:20–09:45 window showing request and 503 time series per client.
- Show a suggested throttling policy for catalog-indexer (example rate / concurrency limits + patch).
Which of the above would you like me to do next?
